b: Just finished up this cabinet and shelves for our living room. We plan to fill it with a turntable, records, and lots of plants.

The cabinet body and shelves are made from cherry veneer plywood. The corners are mitered and the grain wraps around the cabinet body. I had to miter the corners with the track saw since the cabinet was too long for table saw cross-cuts in my small shop. Center divider is constructed with a dado which made assembling such a large cabinet way easier and helped to line up the corners during glue-up.

The cabinet front edges are faced with solid wood cut to a custom 1/2 round profile. To make the face profile strips, I used the router table to round the edge of a larger piece of stock, then ripped the now rounded strip off on the table saw. Doing it this way was much safer and easier that trying to add the round over to a thin strip. To get the face frames mitered perfectly, I used a shooting board to sneak up on the fit.

The circular cabinet door handle is a walnut inlay. This was probably the most complicated part of this project and is difficult to describe briefly. The inlay is two pieces; the outer ring and the back. I cut the outer ring first using a router and a circle jig, then put a chamfer on the backside with the router table. Once the ring profile was cut, I glued on the walnut back and flush cut on the router table to get one circle. I cut a matching circle in the doors while they were still one piece. The whole inlay piece was positioned in the doors before they were cut in half. I used a track saw to cut the doors and the handle in half at the same time so the reveal and the grain match lined up perfectly.

The shelves are mounted to the vertical rails with a sort of half lap/dado joint. This gives them the impression of being semi-floating. The vertical rails are solid cherry. I stuck the two rails together with double-stick tape before cutting the joints so that they would match perfectly. I cut these on the table saw with a crosscut sled. The shelf edges are finished with shop made edge banding veneer. I ironed the edge banding on using regular wood glue.

The vertical rails don't line up with the studs, so they are hung from a horizonal piece of solid wood using a big sliding dovetail. The cabinet is mounted with a French cleat. The shelves and rails have no glue or hardware, just friction fit.
All parts finished with Osmo PolyX clear. This was a super fun project and the first one since remodeling my shop.
